hook.text: Your offer letter says '10,000 stock options.' Is that a lot? A little? It depends on the total shares outstanding.

buildup.text: Options give you the right to buy shares at a fixed 'strike price.' If the company grows, those options become valuable.

discovery.text: Options are worthless until 'exercised'—you pay the strike price to buy real shares, then sell them at market value.

twist.text: If you leave, many companies give you just 90 days to exercise. That means paying taxes and cash you might not have.

climax.text: ISOs get capital gains tax treatment. NSOs are taxed as income.

punchline.text: Options aren't money—they're the right to buy money later.

quiz.question: What is a stock option?
options: The right to buy shares at a predetermined price
